chunks: Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'If I were to feed a needy believer, it would be more beloved to me than if I were to visit him; and if I were to visit him, it would be more beloved to me than if I were to free ten necks (slaves).'
ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved act of charity to the Imams according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy of merit, placing the provision of sustenance to a needy believer above mere social visitation, and visitation above the manumission of ten slaves. This ranking underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on active, material support (sadaqah) as a more profound act of spiritual service than ritualistic or social gestures, reflecting the practical ethic of community care central to Imami tradition. The comparison to freeing slaves highlights the enduring value of personal presence and direct assistance in alleviating human suffering.
